title: The 5 Levels of Self-Driving Production — Eric Schwartz, Traversal
talk_summary: A product manager pitches Traversal's AI SRE platform, framing incident response as a 5-level autonomy ladder from manual war rooms to closed-loop self-healing production. The only concrete mechanisms are a 'production world model' mapping entity relationships across logs/metrics/spans plus a 'causal search engine' harness for agents, with claims of 80%+ root-cause accuracy and 3-minute RCA posts.

takeaways.technique: Production world model (entity-relationship map over operational data)
takeaways.what_they_do: Before searching, they ingest logs/spans/metrics/events and build an explicit map of relationships between entities, so agents navigate a graph instead of grepping raw data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: how do we map out all the relationships between all the dent the data that we're ingesting?
takeaways.numbers: trillions of logs, trillions of spans, tens of billions of metrics

takeaways.technique: First-responder triage agent that pre-investigates before paging humans
takeaways.what_they_do: An agent is dispatched the moment an incident is declared and posts a detailed analysis within minutes, so only 1-2 teams get paged instead of 5-10.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the second the incident is declared traversal is dispatched within 3 minutes we'll post a very detailed root cause analysis
takeaways.numbers: 50+ engineers not paged; 60 min to resolution before; 3 min RCA

takeaways.technique: Alert-noise reduction into a prioritized, pre-investigated queue
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of a raw backlog of hundreds of alerts per engineer, they filter, prioritize, pre-investigate, and route each item to dismiss / fix-rule / create-ticket.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of each engineer having a backlog of 700 alerts, they get a very pri a prioritized and filtered set of alerts that have already been pre-investigated
takeaways.numbers: 700 alerts backlog per engineer reduced to prioritized set

takeaways.what_they_do: They apply the same causal analysis pre-merge to check whether a change makes the system more or less resilient, not just whether it is correct.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when you're putting up changes, how do you make sure that this code is making your system more resilient and reliable over time?

takeaways.technique: Latency budget as an adoption gate
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat >5 minutes to first useful answer as failure because humans revert to old habits, making latency a hard product requirement.
takeaways.evidence_quote: anything more than 5 minutes and you've kind of lost the plot
